title: The Ledger of Greywater Bay Again
premise: August Joubert, coroner of Greywater Bay, receives a retainer from a stranger asking him to prove that a murder has not yet happened — the future victim being Councilman Elias Vann, whose death seven years ago August himself certified as accidental drowning. Digging into his own sealed files, August discovers the original autopsy was falsified under pressure from the town's founding family, the Harrows, and that the stranger is Vann's daughter, returned to force the truth into the open before the Harrows can silence her as they silenced her father. As witnesses die in 'accidents' that mirror the old cover-up, August must choose between the loyalty of a lifetime — his friendship with Sheriff Dane Harrow — and the ledger of names he owes the dead. In the climax at the flooded quarry, August trades his own freedom for evidence, testifying to his part in the falsification; the novel ends with Vann's case reopened, Dane arrested, and August burying his career beside the graves he always knew by name.
about_author: Kestrel Reyes is the pen name of a former coastal records clerk who spent a decade handling death certificates in small maritime towns. Their fiction is known for procedural precision and an obsession with paper trails.

chapters.title: Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: August Joubert's POV. A woman calling herself Maren Cole leaves a cash retainer at his office: prove that Elias Vann will not be murdered. August, who certified Vann's drowning seven years ago, assumes a crank or a grief case. The beat is quiet unease — the money is too much, and she knew where the spare key hangs.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: August's POV. He walks the cemetery at dawn, checking Vann's headstone against his memory of the body: wrong shoes, he suddenly recalls, on a man who fished barefoot. Emotional beat: the first crack in seven years of professional certainty, and the guilt of having not looked closer.

chapters.title: The Harrow File
chapters.summary: August's POV, intercut with a 2017 memo. He pulls his sealed copy of the Vann autopsy and finds his own signature on findings he doesn't remember writing — the toxicology page replaced. Beat: cold horror at realizing he was managed, not merely mistaken.

chapters.title: Maren
chapters.summary: Maren Cole's POV. She admits she is Elias Vann's daughter, raised abroad, armed with her father's letters hinting he'd found something in the Harrow shipping accounts. She wants the case reopened before the anniversary gala. Beat: wary alliance formed between two people who both need August's shame.

chapters.title: Dane
chapters.summary: August's POV. Sheriff Dane Harrow — childhood friend, brother of the man who pressured the autopsy — invites him fishing and mentions, lightly, that strangers asking about Vann tend to leave town. Beat: loyalty and threat braided together; August lies to his oldest friend for the first time.

chapters.title: Paper Doesn't Drown
chapters.summary: August's POV. In the county archive basement he finds the Harrow Shipping ledger showing a $200,000 'consulting fee' paid to Vann two weeks before his death. Beat: rising hope — a trail exists — undercut when the archivist who helped him is found dead that night.

chapters.title: The Second Drowning
chapters.summary: August's POV, forensic detail foregrounded. The archivist's death is ruled accidental, but the lungs tell August what they told him seven years ago: this water was poured in after death. Beat: fury hardening into purpose; he photographs everything this time.

chapters.title: What the Town Knew
chapters.summary: Rotating POV across three townsfolk — a diner owner, a retired teacher, a dockhand. Each remembers a fragment of the night Vann died and each chose silence. Beat: the theme lands — power corrupts not by force but by making silence feel like safety.

chapters.title: Alphabetized Secrets
chapters.summary: August's POV. He begins his own ledger: every name, every favor, every file touched by the Harrows over thirty years. Maren helps. Beat: grim intimacy grows between them; the ledger becomes both weapon and confession.

chapters.title: The Gala
chapters.summary: August's POV. At the Harrow anniversary gala he confronts matriarch Odile Harrow, who offers him a bribe wrapped as respect: a wing named for him, his mistakes forgotten. Beat: temptation played straight — his pension, his name, his peace — and he refuses, badly, shaking.

chapters.title: Tail Lights
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Someone runs her car off the coastal road; she survives because she'd already moved her documents. Beat: fear becomes rage; she stops playing investigator and starts playing bait, over August's objection.

chapters.title: The Deputy Who Talked
chapters.summary: Deputy Ilsa Brandt's POV. She was a rookie seven years ago and saw the second car at the quarry. She gives August a statement, then disappears from her shift. Beat: hope and dread in equal measure — the dominoes are falling, some on innocents.

chapters.title: Quarry Water
chapters.summary: August's POV. He dives the old quarry with a salvage friend and finds Vann's truck, and inside it, the missing original toxicology report — Vann was poisoned, then drowned. Beat: vindication shadowed by terror; someone watched them surface.

chapters.title: Brother's Keeper
chapters.summary: Dane Harrow's POV. We see his private war: love for August, loyalty to Odile, and knowledge of exactly who gave the order seven years ago — his late brother, on Odile's instruction. Beat: tragic antagonist fully lit; Dane chooses, for now, to warn August instead of stopping him.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: August's POV. His office is torched overnight; the ledger survives only because he'd begun scanning copies to Maren. The fire marshal calls it electrical. Beat: rock bottom — reputation smeared, license threatened, allies scattering.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Silence
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. They find Deputy Brandt alive but coerced into recanting, held quietly at a Harrow property 'for her safety.' Maren photographs the arrangement. Beat: moral escalation — rescuing Ilsa means crossing lines August swore he wouldn't.

chapters.title: Odile's Version
chapters.summary: Odile Harrow's POV. Her chapter reveals the machinery: the town's economy is Harrow-built, and she believes order justifies burial — literally. She offers Maren the truth plus exile, the same deal once offered Vann. Beat: chilling self-righteousness; the villain thinks she's the load-bearing wall.

chapters.title: The Deal Refused
chapters.summary: August's POV. Maren nearly takes Odile's offer — until August shows her the ledger page with her father's name and the word 'settled' in Odile's hand. Beat: grief transmuted to resolve; the alliance becomes a partnership of equals.

chapters.title: Anniversary Eve
chapters.summary: Rotating short POVs — August, Dane, Maren, Odile — as all four prepare for tomorrow: the reopening petition, the arrest warrant Dane must serve or refuse, the press Maren has summoned. Beat: coiled suspense; every character knows the town changes by nightfall.

chapters.title: The Quarry, Again
chapters.summary: Climax. August's POV. Odile's fixer corners August and Maren at the quarry to destroy the recovered report; Dane arrives, gun drawn, and finally turns it on his own family's man. In the struggle the fixer drowns in the same water — the bay taking its own back. Beat: violent catharsis, morally costly.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: August's POV. Before a packed courthouse and state investigators, August confesses his own falsified signature before presenting the ledger, the report, and Odile's handwriting. Odile is indicted; Dane resigns rather than arrest his mother, then does it anyway. Beat: justice outside the law made lawful at last, at personal ruin.

chapters.title: Closing the Ledger
chapters.summary: August's POV, epilogue tone. Months later: Vann reburied under a corrected stone, Maren leaving with her father's name cleared, August unemployed but unburied. He writes the final entry in the ledger — his own name — and closes it. Beat: bittersweet peace; the cost of truth, paid in full and worth it.
